method: Compared with the pdftotext text layer of the official QP PDF (SHA-256 checked exactly against source.sha256), using -layout, -table and -raw modes (poppler pdftotext was unavailable; xpdf pdftotext was used, whose -table/-raw modes expose stacked-fraction structure that -layout squashes onto one line). The official marking scheme PDF (Physics_UPD_U/Physics/English/XII-2-042-1-1.pdf) was independently checked page by page and confirmed to have no usable text-layer answer content (every page extracts to only 'HOME' navigation links and bare question/option numbers; all answer text, values and working are embedded as images), matching the pack's own note; no officialAnswer could be verified from the scheme for any question.

questions.reason: mu0 (permeability) and pi are missing from options (B)-(D), which should read mu0*I/2*pi*a, mu0*I/4*pi*a, mu0*I/6*pi*a; kept as extracted with the symbols dropped to blanks/'0'.

questions.reason: Option (C) is a genuine stacked fraction '5' over '2' V in the PDF (i.e. 5/2 V), but the pack stores it as '52 V', which reads as the unrelated number 52. Options (B)/(D) are missing the radical sign (almost certainly 5*sqrt(2) V / 10*sqrt(2) V).

questions.reason: Options (A) and (C) are genuine stacked fractions in the PDF -- (A) = d/2, (C) = d/4 -- but the pack stores them as '2d' and '4d', duplicating options (B) and (D) so all four options read as only two distinct values.
questions.notes: -table mode shows unambiguously: (A) d over 2, (B) 2d, (C) d over 4, (D) 4d. questions.reason: omega (angular frequency) is missing throughout the four wave equations (i)-(iv), and pi is very likely missing before '/3' in option (iv) (sin(omega*t + pi/3)); kept as extracted with these symbols dropped.

The stem says the heaters are connected 'across a dc source of 2V volt', but the PDF text layer shows a genuine stacked fraction 'V' over '2' at that point, i.e. the source is V/2 volt, not 2V. This changes the numeric problem materially.
questions.notes: Cross-check: solving with the two candidate source voltages, only Vs = V/2 reduces to the clean closed form P1*P2/(4*(P1+P2)), which is exactly option (D) as extracted; Vs = 2V does not match any of the four printed options, strongly confirming V/2 is correct and the pack's '2V' is wrong. Options (B)-(D) are also fractions with lost fraction bars, kept as extracted.
